sentences.text: Pelagosaurus was a small reptile, typically measuring less than 2 meters in length.

The holotype specimen of Pelagosaurus typus was discovered north of Ilminster in Somerset, England, while remains including skulls and articulated skeletons have been found in France, Germany, and Switzerland.
A 2006 dissertation listed a total of 88 Pelagosaurus specimens.
Several juvenile specimens provide insight into the growth patterns of Pelagosaurus.
Pelagosaurus fed on fish, crustaceans, and insects, with one juvenile specimen found containing a primitive teleost fish in its stomach.

Later analyses consistently classify Pelagosaurus as a basal metriorhynchoid, a group of fully pelagic crocodyliforms with flippered limbs and smooth skin, and it is classified within the family Teleosauridae.
Pelagosaurus is an extinct marine crocodile relative that lived approximately 183 to 176 million years ago during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
Pelagosaurus inhabited shallow epicontinental seas covering much of modern-day Western Europe.

The evolutionary placement of Pelagosaurus within Thalattosuchia has historically been a subject of debate, though recent phylogenetic analyses suggest Pelagosaurus was a primitive teleosaurid rather than a basal metriorhynchid or thalattosuchian.
